# SPE Round 3 Plan

Round 2 went badly for the predictions. One of five cells was a hit. In the other four, the naive guess "same as last round" was closer than my number. So this round starts from the round 2 measured values. I move a number only when a failure ID gives a reason.

I used two defaults to fill gaps in what you pasted. First, the original ticket set is 30 tickets (T01 to T30). Second, any cell without a pasted round 2 baseline is held at its round 2 measured value. I will read those values from the round 2 results when I write `r03.yaml`.

## 1. Specify

### Decisions on the round 3 proposals

| ID | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Adopt | This is the fix for F4. It is the only change to config C. |
| P2 | Adopt, with a different reason | 0.86 is not a ceiling. The real reason is that mixed billing and outage tickets are where F4 shows up. The 10 new tickets are a separate set, H01 to H10. Their scores are never pooled with the original set, so the round 2 baselines stay comparable. |
| P3 | Rejected by default. Open decision D1. | Dropping D loses the cheap baseline. F6 has a direct fix that can be tested. My default is to keep D and cap its retries. |
| P4 | Adopt | B's round 2 miss was inside the noise at n=3. |

### Round 3 requirements (for `spe/spec/spec.md`)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R3.1 | Config C moves the outage status check into its own tool. The other merged tools stay as they are. | r02 F4, P1 | Code check. On every outage ticket, C's tool log shows the status check was called. |
| R3.2 | Add 10 tickets, H01 to H10, that mix billing and outage problems. Their gold labels follow the rule in D2. | P2 | Results for this set are reported on their own and never pooled with T01 to T30. |
| R3.3 | Run 5 trials per cell instead of 3. | P4, r02 B miss | The completeness critic confirms 5 valid trials per cell, or logs the voids and skips. |
| R3.4 | Config D allows at most 1 retry per trial. Nothing else in D changes. | r02 F6, D1 default | Code check. Each D trial makes 1 retry or fewer. |
| R3.5 | The grader reads priority from `label.priority` only. | r02 F5 | A selftest case has a draft reply that says P1 and a label that says P3. The grader must score P3. |
| R3.6 | Configs A and B do not change. A is the control. | Rule: one change per config | A diff of the A and B config files against r02 is empty. |
| R3.7 | Paid spend is capped at $25 for the round. | Default | The harness skips any trial that would cross the cap and logs it. |

### Open decisions (for `spe/spec/disagreements.md`)

| ID | Question | Owner | Default if you do not answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Should we drop config D, or fix its retries? | You | Keep D and cap retries at 1. Saying "drop D" removes 200 trials. |
| D2 | What is the gold category for a ticket that has both a billing problem and an outage? | You | The category is whichever problem blocks the customer right now. If service is down, outage wins. |

## 2. Predict

The hit tolerance is ±0.01 for accuracy and ±$0.0005 for cost. This matches round 2, so the verdicts compare across rounds. With 150 trials per config, the standard error for accuracy is about ±0.03. That means ±0.01 is tighter than the noise. I will report a 95% interval next to each measured value. The hit rule stays the same.

### Original set (T01 to T30)

| Metric | A | B | C | D | Grader check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| category accuracy | 0.86 | 0.86 | 0.80 | 0.74 | `grade.py`: exact match of `label.category` against the gold label |
| priority accuracy | r02 value | r02 value | **0.76** (was 0.71) | r02 value | `grade.py`: `label.priority` against the gold label (the F5 fix) |
| cost per ticket | r02 value | r02 value | r02 value | **$0.003** (was $0.004) | API usage tokens × the price table, mean per ticket |

**Why each row:**
- **Category accuracy.** I hold every config at its round 2 value. A and B did not change. F4 is about priority, so I have no evidence that splitting out the outage tool changes C's category accuracy.
- **Priority accuracy.** F4 sent outage tickets to P3 because C never called the status check. Splitting the tool back out should fix those tickets. My round 2 moves overshot, so I move C only part of the way back toward round 1's 0.78. The other configs did not change, so I hold them.
- **Cost per ticket.** F6 doubled the tokens on long tickets through retries. Capping retries at 1 should bring D back to round 1's $0.003. C's extra tool might add a few tokens, but I have no basis to put a number on it, so I hold C.

### Hard set (H01 to H10), category accuracy

| A | B | C | D |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.70 | 0.70 | 0.64 | 0.58 |

**Why:** This set has no baseline. I subtract one shared drop of 0.16 from each config's original-set number and keep the round 2 gaps between configs. I am not confident in these four numbers. The harness reports priority on the hard set but I do not predict it.

## 3. Evaluate

### Gates before launch (any failure halts the run and I report back)

1. **Grader selftest.** The oracle answers must pass. Empty and wrong answers must fail. The R3.5 conflict case must score P3.
2. **Control regrade.** I regrade the r02 transcripts with the current `grade.py`. The results must reproduce the regraded r02 numbers: category A 0.86, B 0.86, C 0.80, D 0.74, and priority C 0.71.
3. **Answer key check.** All 10 hard-set gold labels exist. They sit outside every path a trial can read.
4. **Dry run on 3 cells, 1 trial each:**
   - C on T17 checks that the status check gets called.
   - D on the longest ticket checks that retries stay at 1 or fewer.
   - A on H01 checks that the hard set loads and grades.

### Workflow arguments

```js
const ROUND = 3;
args = {
  configs: ["A", "B", "C", "D"],
  ticketSets: { original: "T01..T30", hard: "H01..H10" },
  trialsPerCell: 5,
  splitCellExtraTrials: 3,
  budgetCapUSD: 25,
  trialSchema: { ticket_id, label: { category, priority }, draft_reply, tool_calls, tokens }
}
```

### Run steps

1. Run 4 configs × 40 tickets × 5 trials, which is 800 trials. Every prompt takes the round from `ROUND`.
2. Run the code checks first: category, priority, cost, the F4 status-check detector, and the F6 retry counter. Every metric here can be checked by code, so no trial needs a judge.
3. Scan every transcript for reads of `grade.py`, the gold files, or `spe/predictions/`. Void any trial that touched them and count the voids.
4. A split cell is one where the 5 trials disagree, such as 3 to 2. Each split cell gets up to 3 more trials, within the budget.
5. Track spend as the run goes. Skip any trial that would cross $25 and log the skip.
6. Run failure analysis. Each miss maps to F4, F6, or a new F number.
7. Run the completeness critic. It confirms every predicted cell has a measured value and lists all voids and skips.

### Cost estimate (not measured)

- Agent cost for A, B, and C: about 600 trials × $0.01 = $6.00. This assumes $0.01 per ticket, because the round 2 cost for A to C was not in what you pasted.
- Agent cost for D: about 200 trials × $0.003 = $0.60.
- Failure analysis and the completeness critic: about $2.
- **Total: about $9 against a $25 cap.**

## 4. After approval, in this order (with local commits only, no push)

1. Save your prompt verbatim to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r03.md`. Add the R3 table to `spe/spec/spec.md` and add D1 and D2 to `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. Commit `SPE r03 specify`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r03.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r03.yaml` with round, date, author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", configs, the numbers, a Why per number, and `same_as_last_round`. Its first line is `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` Leave `r03-draft.yaml` as it is. Commit `SPE r03 predict: hold baselines, C priority 0.76, D cost $0.003`.
3. Write `spe/evals/harness/r03-workflow.js`, update `grade.py` for the selftest case, and add the hard-set tickets and key. Commit `SPE r03 evaluate (harness)`.
4. Run the gates, then launch the Workflow. When the completion notice arrives, commit `SPE r03 evaluate (results): <headline>`.
5. Close out the round:
   - Add the round 3 rows and "Which Why broke" to `spe/prediction-log.md`.
   - Add new F numbers to `spe/failures.md`, with original and regraded numbers side by side. Update the Fix field for F4 and F6.
   - Add "Proposed for round 4" to the spec and write `r04-draft.yaml`.
   - Update `spe/README.md`.
   - Commit `SPE r03 learn` and tag `spe-r03`.

**Stop rule status:** 0 rounds in a row have matched. The run halts on the budget cap, a leaked answer key, a failed grader gate, or D1 or D2 if your answer changes the plan.
critiques: The plan is titled "SPE Round 3 Plan". It opens with a Specify phase that rules on the round 3 proposals and adds R3 requirements. The agent treated "ok, next one" as the start of a new round with a respec, and nobody had to name the phase.

The decisions table covers all four proposals. P1 is adopted as the F4 fix. P2 is adopted with a corrected reason. P3 is rejected by default and opened as D1. P4 is adopted because the miss is inside noise at n=3.
R3.1 cites "r02 F4". R3.4 cites "r02 F6". R3.5 cites "r02 F5". Each failure ID is tied to a requirement.

The prediction does start from round 2 measured values ("hold every config at its round 2 value"). The only band is one global hit tolerance of ±0.01 / ±$0.0005. The answer itself admits this is "tighter than the noise", so it is not a real band on each number. Several cells read "r02 value" and have no number at all. That means not every number has a band.

A "Why each row" section explains category, priority, and cost. It names the specific moves (C priority 0.76 from F4, D cost $0.003 from F6) and the reason the other cells are held. The hard-set numbers have their own Why (a shared 0.16 drop that keeps the round 2 gaps).

Step 2 of "After approval" writes spe/predictions/r03.yaml with a do-not-edit header and commits it as "SPE r03 predict". The harness is written in step 3 and the run launches in step 4. So the prediction is committed before any trial.

"Gates before launch" lists a grader selftest, a control regrade of the r02 transcripts with expected numbers, an answer key check, and a 3-cell dry run. Any gate failure halts the run before the full 800-trial run.
